sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter is called (гэ) /ɡɛ/. Its main sound is heard in the word (город) /ˈɡorət/, which means city, town. This letter can make four different sounds in Russian words.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Press the back of your tongue against the soft roof of your mouth. Release the air with your voice on. Next, raise the middle of your tongue toward the hard roof while keeping that back contact. For the third sound, keep your mouth the same but turn your voice off. For the last sound, touch your top teeth to your lower lip and breathe out. Touch your throat to feel the voice shake.

sections.title: Reading this letter
paragraphs: The hard sound /ɡ/ appears before hard vowels and voiced consonants, as in (глаз) /ɡlas/. You hear the soft sound /ɡʲ/ before soft vowels, as in (где) /ɡʲdʲe/. At the end of a word or before voiceless consonants, the sound becomes /k/, as in (друг) /druk/. In common adjective and pronoun word endings, the letter sounds like /v/, as in (его) /jɪˈvo/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not let this consonant slide into an English h sound. Keep the back of your tongue pressed firmly against the roof of your mouth, just like the g in go. Remember to say the sound of v in vine when you read the special word endings.
